text:
Auscultation of the neck is not necessary when examining the jugular venous pulse; the exam relies on inspection of the venous waveform with the patient at 30–45 degrees. Assessing height, waveform, and hepatojugular reflux are relevant, but auscultation is not part of the assessment. Note that the internal jugular vein, not the external, is generally preferred for accurate JVP evaluation.
CONFIDENCE: 85
